hypothesis: Repairing loop-start metadata in the acyclic producer rejection fixture makes exact original-loop diagnostics testable without changing the compiler transformation. The inherited extension admits bounded canonical branch-only DAG producers with serial, nested, asymmetric or cross-edge control and unconditional latch integer-add or ordered float/double-add recurrences. Scalar producers and independently vectorized consumers remain possible without a VPlan for the original loop, a new profitability model, pressure thresholds or numerical relaxation.
semantics: For multiblock loops, hasAcyclicProducerCFG requires a unique exiting latch and BranchInst terminators. All non-latch successor edges must stay in the loop and cannot target its header. It counts incoming edges with the latch backedge/exit excluded, then performs an iterative Kahn traversal seeded only by the header. Visiting every loop block proves both reachability and absence of internal cycles. Every non-latch node has a successor in this finite DAG, so the latch is the only sink: every iteration reaches it exactly once. Duplicate successor edges are counted/decremented separately. Single-block loops retain the old fast path and later exit diagnostics. Existing simplify-form, dedicated-exit, LCSSA, unique-exit, canonical-zero/one-IV, invariant equality-bound and finite SCEV trip checks still apply. Newly admitted unconditional updates must reside in the latch; existing narrow header-update cases remain supported. Conditional backedge PHIs require the unchanged single triangle/diamond recognizer before participation analysis, so a two-input merge in a larger serial/nested CFG cannot acquire a counter that assumes one participation arm. All rejections precede mutation. Emission is unchanged: original branches, contribution PHIs, arm-local loads/divisions and safe helper calls remain in place, with distinct available contribution values stored at the latch under the original iteration index. Consumer updates are cloned, preserving add flags, FP operand order and per-reduction iteration order. No inactive zero arithmetic or speculative arm evaluation is introduced. Header/update use restrictions preserve reduction-feedback rejection, and only final reduction results may escape through the original exit. Other live-outs, stores, volatile/atomic accesses, unsupported instructions and unsafe calls remain rejected. Calls still require the explicit direct memory(none), nounwind, willreturn, speculatable and other existing effect contracts; no libm-name or errno assumptions are added. Input/output aliasing and enclosing-loop row stores retain their original producer/consumer sequencing. Ordinary ordered FP is unchanged under both settings of the separate fission FP-reordering option; strictfp functions and constrained FP remain rejected. Executable verification is requested through the extended existing checker, not claimed run. Three mixed acyclic producers and an enclosing-loop producer are compiled both as untouched original scalar IR and actual transformed stages, with independent C scalar formulas as a second reference. The checker verifies exact source-location Selected, producer VF 1, consumer VF vscale x 4, capacity/bytes, preserved producer edges/PHIs and arm-local operations, shared slots and ordered consumer reductions. Host-only probes are inserted after PHIs in exact producer header, latch, vector-consumer header and scalar tail. Expected visits are N, N, floor(N/VF), N%VF, summed per row for enclosing loops. Mixed cases exercise every N=0..65, invalid 66/UINT64_MAX, positive/negative nonzero divisors, all-load/all-division (null FP input), alternating phases, runs, sparse/random branches and nested branch combinations. Inputs are preserved, output canaries checked, and repeated/alias invocations compare integer and ordered non-NaN FP bits, signed zero included; NaNs compare by classification without inventing payload guarantees. Enclosing loops use zero/one/four and invalid rows, initial/carry/export state, exact stage visits, independent unaliased/aliased C references and future-row input aliasing. One and two ordinary LV invocations, both FP option settings and vscales 1/2/4/8/32 are covered. Additional actual scalar-stage comparisons execute 1, 255 and 16384 trips, including the full default scratch capacity, against original IR and independent formulas with exact producer/latch/consumer counts. Existing executable cases and correctness assertions are retained. This revision changes only fixture debug metadata and validation assertions. Every preheader now carries its original loop-start location; the outer cycle also has that location in its loop ID, while the inner self-loop has a distinct location. Exact rejection assertions are unchanged. Native output additionally proves that the outer and inner backedges remain and contains no scalar-fission stages. The acyclic proof, latch-update restriction, narrow participation recognizer, emission, ordered FP contract, alias behavior, live-out restrictions and bounded scratch implementation are untouched.
costs: Let M be the proven maximum trip count, N the actual count, and S the sum of allocation sizes of distinct contribution SSA values. Static entry scratch remains M*S plus existing ABI alignment padding, checked by existing unsigned arithmetic, IV representability, pointer-index bounds and the 65536-byte default per-candidate ceiling. It can reserve stack space even on a guarded bypass. Three mixed fixtures each use one 65*i32, one 65*double and one 65*float array for four reductions (shared integer contribution): 1044 accounted bytes including 4 padding bytes; logical stores 16*N bytes and loads 16*N bytes, total 32*N. The enclosing producer uses 784 accounted bytes (65*i32 plus 65*double and 4 padding bytes), reused across rows, with 12*N stores and 12*N loads per row. Capacity does not multiply by row count. Scalar boundary execution uses 4, 1020 and 65536 scratch bytes for M=1,255,16384; tests reject the 256-trip i8 overflow and 16385*i32 byte excess before mutation, and a 3-byte ceiling rejects every fixture in that boundary file. There are zero added original-input rereads, duplicated producer operations or recomputed contributions, no participation/mask arrays for these unconditional streams, and no new per-iteration producer branch or counter. Existing producer iteration guards stay in place; the existing extra consumer loop/control and ordinary LV vector/tail checks remain. There are no new alias or SCEV guards, unbounded/dynamic allocation, path enumeration, if-conversion or generic dependence machinery. The added admission check uses O(B+E) time and O(B) temporary compiler memory (E<=2B for branches), iterative rather than recursive; existing instruction/use scans, SCEV analysis and full-function dominator recalculation are unchanged. Narrow compact recognition remains a separate constant-size check. Host probes/reference formulas increase validation cost only and are excluded from RVV codegen inputs. Physical stack padding/cache traffic, register pressure and speedups have not been measured. The t000017 repair adds no runtime operations, scratch, traffic, rereads, duplicated computations, guards or compiler analysis. It only adds debug locations and regression assertions/artifacts. The inherited O(B+E)-time, O(B)-space CFG admission and existing scratch bounds are unchanged.

revision_repair.root_cause: Loop::getLocRange, used by getStartLoc, consults DILocation operands in the loop ID, then the preheader terminator, then the header terminator. The original fixture supplied only latch !dbg, which is not a fallback for a multiblock header. The historical diagnostic dump therefore contains <unknown>:0:0 even though its rejection reasons are correct.
revision_repair.fix: Give all twelve original loop preheader terminators their existing exact loop-start DILocation. Preserve all latch locations and all eleven REASON filename/line/column/reason assertions. Add the existing outer 22:3 DILocation to the cyclic outer loop ID while preserving its vectorize.enable and width=2 hints. Give the inner self-loop its own 25:5 DILocation and loop ID, so it cannot stand in for the outer diagnostic.
revision_repair.native_worklist_argument: collectSupportedLoops selects the reducible explicitly hinted outer loop when enable-vplan-native-path is enabled and returns without collecting its inner loop. runImpl forms LCSSA recursively, then invokes scalar fission before ordinary LV legality. The outer unique-latch CFG still contains the inner self-cycle after excluding the outer backedge. Kahn traversal cannot consume that inner self-edge and must reject the original outer at 22:3 with scalar-unsupported-cfg. This is a source-derived expectation, pending harness execution.
